summary:
George Hill (1750–1819) was a Scottish minister and academic who led the Church of Scotland’s Moderate party after Principal William Robertson’s death. Born in St Andrews, he graduated from its university at 14 and became professor of Greek in 1772. He was ordained in 1778 and appointed to a St Andrews ministry in 1780, later becoming professor of divinity and, in 1791, principal of St Mary’s College. He also served as dean of the Chapel Royal and the Order of the Thistle.

Hill helped found the Royal Society of Edinburgh in 1783 and was Moderator of the General Assembly in 1789. A skilled speaker and church politician, he accepted landowners’ role in appointing ministers but strongly defended the Church’s independence from government. During the French Revolutionary Wars, he opposed using pulpits to promote a voluntary levy. A Whig who feared popular unrest, he also opposed Catholic emancipation. Ill health curtailed his public work from 1807; he died in St Andrews in 1819.
